summary: Singly-linked-list removal by node value. Walks the list from *this (head) matching the node whose +0x0 value equals a2, splices it out (updating head, tail at this[1], and current-cursor this[2]), decrements the count at this[0xC], optionally clears the +0x8 byte, frees the node value if that +0x8 byte is set, then frees the node itself via FreeWrapper_7bcf and returns 1. Returns 0 when a2 is zero, the list is empty, or no node matches.

operations.description: If a2 (the value to remove) is zero, return 0 immediately without touching the list.
Initialize walker v4 = *this (head node) and previous-pointer v5 = 0.
If *this (head) is null, the list is empty; return 0.
Traverse the chain: while the current node's +0x0 value differs from a2, advance v5 = v4 and v4 = *(v4 + 4) (next pointer); if v4 becomes null, the value is absent and the function returns 0.
If the matched node is the current cursor this[2], move the cursor to the node's next pointer.
Splice out the matched node: capture its next pointer, link previous node's +0x4 to it; if there is no previous node, update the head *this to the next pointer.
If the matched node is the tail this[1], move the tail back to the previous node v5 (which is 0 when removing the only element).
Decrement the node count at this[0xC].
If the a3 flag is zero, clear the matched node's +0x8 byte.
If the matched node's +0x8 byte is set and its +0x0 value is non-null, free the value via FreeWrapper_7bcf before freeing the node itself.
Free the matched node itself via FreeWrapper_7bcf.
Return 1 to signal a successful removal (and 0 on all early-exit paths).
